findings.location: client/src/pages/Panel.validation.test.js:190-195 (describe("validateDiscountFields") > "rejects empty and non-numeric input instead of coercing it to 0")
findings.issue: This test only feeds bad/non-numeric values ("", "   ", "abc", null, undefined, NaN) into min_qty and percent — never into max_qty. Reading the implementation (Panel.jsx, validateDiscountFields): `if (!isPositiveNumber(fields.max_qty)) { errors.max_qty = ... } else if (isPositiveNumber(fields.min_qty) && toFiniteNumber(fields.max_qty) < toFiniteNumber(fields.min_qty)) { errors.max_qty = ... }`. The first branch (`!isPositiveNumber(fields.max_qty)`) is the only thing that rejects a non-numeric max_qty, because `toFiniteNumber("abc") < toFiniteNumber(min_qty)` evaluates to `NaN < 11` which is `false` and would silently NOT flag the row in the else-if branch alone. I applied the litmus test: if that first `if` block were deleted (leaving only the `else if` comparison), a discount tier with `max_qty: "abc"` and any valid min_qty would incorrectly validate as `{ valid: true }` (since NaN comparisons are always false) — and no test in the current suite would catch that regression, because every existing max_qty-related test (`rejects max_qty < min_qty`, `accepts a fully valid tier`) only ever supplies numeric max_qty values.
